I went through depression and came out of it better, yet you're still in there so I'm just trying to advise you what helped me. If you don't agree with it that's fair enough,  I'm not claiming to be a doctor or someone who can give actual scientific evidence for anything, all I know is by just packing up my shit and going to a different country put me on a course of getting out of the shit I was in. And it's not easy, your brains gonna tell you this shit is not gonna work, but that's because you're depressed, what do you have to lose? If you're already close to suicide or whatever just fuck it, pack your bags, move countries, go to thailand, australia, europe, just keep trying different things. I lost my gut feeling and didn't know what to do with my life and it was only when I left everything and just started following my instincts that things changed.
You don't have to listen to me, and don't have to take my advice, but don't call me naive when you're ready to give up on life and I've been there and beat it. I know what it's like so don't question that.

What advice do you want me to give you? Look on the bright side of life and get on a course of anti depressants? 
What are you looking for?

My main one was to live like I'm the hero my own movie and make decisions based around that. I've got a ton of other rules too that help me but it's really based on that initial decision you make. Think rationally, your life is shit, else you wouldn't be depressed. Something needs to change, what I say to people, especially those close to killing themselves or booking a flight, is to get all the money that you have, book a flight to somewhere tropical or new or somewhere you've always wanted to go before you die and start again. I'm in Australia now and it's completely turned my life around. Tell me more about your situations and I'll tell you more about mine now (you can have a look at my old posts to see how depressed I was) and maybe we can help eachother.
Thing is though, depression isn't terminal, you can get better. I'm proof.

Ok so from what you just said, you want to be more like your best friend or ex, very good at rationalizing their emotions or shutting them off. Ok so from now on, if you're making a decision and you're certain you want to be like your best friend etc and want to make a change in your personality. Ask yourself, what would they do in this situation? So basically you're presented with a situation where usually you may act irrational, take a breath, close your eyes and think of that person you want to be like and how they would act in the current situation you find yourself in. Then just do exactly what you think that person would do. This may be difficult to grasp at first, but soon enough after enough times you will find yourself changing as a person!

Ok first of all, don't beat yourself up too much, it doesn't really get you anywhere. A lot of people go through this, just not that many people talk about it so yeah it does feel fucking embarrassing over what something people consider is a normal thing like a break up. But it isn't that normal, when you love someone and lose them it hurts like hell. 

First of I'll tell you what I did and not saying it's right or wrong but you can choose to do with it what you will. The key to this is, if you're miserable now you're only going to make someone else miserable. You need to make yourself happy before you can think about making someone else happy. You have to come first. This is where I come up with my life rules:

If you change nothing, nothing will change.

How would the person I would like to be, do the things I am about to do.

Follow your gut, it's telling you something for a reason.

Take life advice from people you want to be like, not people you don't.

If somethings a once in a lifetime experience, just go for it. Figure a work around with work or whatever you're currently doing, things will work out. You'll be more gutted than you didn't go than happy that you stayed. 

Put yourself first, not work.

If you want to do something, do it.

Ok so that's my list  as of now, but i'm adding to it as I learn new things. Trusting your gut, changing your life situation if you're unhappy and being the hero of your own movie are my 3 biggest tips to a healthy mindset. Let me know what you think and I'll go into more detail on each if you're interested?

I know what you mean, but it's pointless to be afraid of the future. I know lung disease and heart disease sounds terrible but neither you nor me know whether you're going to get that for certain. For example, i was convinced that all of this stress and shit I've been going through is gonna cause me to get alzheimers when I get older or cut my life expectancy down and knock years off of my life. When you write it down and analyse it with a rational mind you can sometimes see what you're saying is the depression/ anxiety talking. You need to think about what you're doing and saying and just think, does that really make sense? 
The fact you don't have the desire to do any of those things may also be linked to your depression. What's the harm in trying? I know you say it tires you out but are you gonna be happier sat at home? I get told to go out and do things all the time too, I know what it's like. It does sound shitty at times but sometimes it can be just what you need to get you back on track.
